svg.text: Complete CI/CD Pipeline — Java Maven App on AWS EC2
GitHub → Jenkins → Docker Hub → SSH/Docker Compose → EC2, with loop-safe auto-versioning
reads new version from pom.xml → env.IMAGE_NAME = version-BUILD_NUMBER
⚠ single-quoted to survive bash + Groovy parsing
mvn clean package → compile, test, jar
docker login → docker push → docker image prune -f
prune prevents the disk-fill incident from recurring
⚠ IMAGE_NAME passed as $1, not hardcoded — always deploys the
exact version just built and pushed
git commit -m "ci: version bump [skip ci]" → git push origin HEAD:main
loop guard catches it on the next run, back at the top
re-triggers webhook → loop guard checks again
SSH private key → sshagent for deploy
and re-paste the full key if this recurs
Real incidents this pipeline design protects against
• Disk fill-up from 45+ leftover images during an earlier un-guarded loop → now prevented by [skip ci] + docker image prune -f
• Port collisions on redeploy from unnamed containers → now handled automatically by Docker Compose's service tracking
• Filename mismatches (docker-compose.yml vs .yaml) caused two separate scp failures → fixed by matching names exactly
• Wrong image referenced in compose file (demo-app vs testing-app) caused "manifest unknown" → fixed by matching what's actually pushed
• [skip ci] text present but unchecked once caused the loop to return → the Stage 0 check must exist, not just the commit marker
Debugging habit that mattered most: isolating failing commands by running them directly over SSH, outside Jenkins, to prove
whether a bug lived in bash/Maven/Docker itself — or in the pipeline wrapping it.
copied fresh from Jenkins workspace on every deploy
present if the app's data layer is wired up
